svg.text: The article is a chain running from what silk is and how it behaves, through how spiders make it, to how humans
try to copy and use it — each stage building on the last.

g.text: Spider silk: from web to lab
A chain down the page: silk's biology and properties lead to its natural production, then to artificial copying, then
to human application; research and references sit as apparatus alongside.

g.title: Silk's many jobs for spiders — prey, shelter, mating, food — → spya-gp4t9x
Structure gives it strength and stretch — crystal sheets + stretchy matrix — → spya-py9zw6
Many ecological uses — capture, dispersal, nests, signals — → spya-rty5kb
Different glands, different silks — dragline, capture-spiral, wrap, glue — → spya-hg7j7e
Spun on demand through a tapering duct — liquid protein → solid fibre — → spya-g3h8qq
One spider, hundreds of glands — garden cross spider example — → spya-zrcs7h
Copying silk is still hard — feedstock + duct both needed — → spya-d7d7m8
Decades of mapping silk's science — chemistry, genes, mechanics — → spya-jvxbb8
Human uses: cloth, medicine, tech — rare textile, wound dressing, optics — → spya-chy97m
References & related topics — → spya-jdybu5
